newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SAMPRAS RETIRES WITH STRAINED THIGH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS RETIRES WITH STRAINED THIGH.

text.p: Pete Sampras had to retire from his opening match of the World Team Cup against Australia's Mark Philippoussis on Monday after straining a left thigh muscle.
World number one Sampras was leading 6-4 4-6 1-0 when he began to experience pain in the same leg that hampered him at the Italian Open in Rome.
Sampras was examined by tournament doctor Hartmut Krahl, who diagnosed the problem as a strain in the upper-left thigh.
"I don't know whether I'll be able to play again on Wednesday," said Sampras after receiving ultra-sound treatment. "I had problems like this in Rome but it was on the other side of the thigh."
If Sampras is unable to compete, his place in the United States team will be taken by Alex O'Brien, who is already playing in the doubles with Jonathan Stark.
With the Americans down a match, Michael Chang levelled the tie against Australia at 1-1 when he beat Mark Woodforde 6-3 4-6 7-5.
The deciding doubles match between O'Brien and Stark and the world number one doubles team of Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge will be played on Tuesday.
The match was put back a day to allow O'Brien time to reach the tournament after competing on the final day of the Italian Open on Sunday.
Paul Haarhuis led the Netherlands to a 2-1 win over Germany in the day's other tie.
Germany began positively, with Michael Stich beating Jan Siemerink 6-3 6-2.
But Haarhuis levelled the tie with a 7-5 6-4 win over David Prinosil, then joined Jacco Eltingh to beat Stich and Martin Sinner 6-2 6-3.
